booking-com.name: Booking.com
booking-com.key_insight: Booking.com is arguably the most aggressive deployer of behavioral design patterns in consumer tech — and uniquely, they've been transparent about it. The platform runs over 1,000 A/B tests simultaneously, and the result is a UI so dense with urgency signals that it has become a case study in regulatory behavioral design complaints. 'Only 2 rooms left!' '14 people looking right now!' 'Booked 3 times in the last 24 hours!' — each message exploits a different psychological lever (scarcity, social proof, loss aversion). The EU fined Booking.com in 2020 for misleading urgency claims, yet the patterns persist because they work. The ethical tension is stark: Booking.com's design genuinely helps users make faster decisions in a complex market (hotels have variable pricing, real scarcity), but the same urgency cues are applied indiscriminately — to fully available hotels and nearly-sold-out ones alike. When scarcity signals are always on, they become manipulation rather than information. Booking.com represents what happens when conversion optimization is pursued without ethical guardrails.

figma.name: Figma
figma.key_insight: Figma is the most elegant example of network-effect behavioral design in B2B software. Every design decision serves a single behavioral insight: make collaboration so effortless that the tool becomes the team's shared space, not just one designer's workspace. The cursor presence feature (seeing teammates' cursors labeled with their names in real-time) is pure social facilitation — knowing someone is watching you work changes how you work. The generous free tier isn't charity — it's a viral acquisition mechanism: every designer who opens a Figma link to view a prototype becomes a potential user. Figma's file-sharing is designed like Google Docs, not like Photoshop: no installation, no file format confusion, no version control headaches. By eliminating every friction point in collaboration, Figma made itself structurally impossible to replace — switching to a competitor means convincing your entire team, your clients, and your developer handoff workflow to switch simultaneously. This is behavioral lock-in through genuine value creation, not dark patterns.
figma.top_technique: Multiplayer Cursor Presence as Social Facilitation
